groups.title: checker.py: CLI and check() that grade a text submission against a quest's acceptance criteria

checks.why: check() against the summary quest, pass and fail
the CLI end to end on files in the repo (exit 0 only if all criteria pass; here it is expected to exit 1)

risks.text: The CLI reads the submission with open().read(): no explicit encoding (platform default) and trailing newline/whitespace kept, so a file saved with a final newline counts one extra character in max_chars/min_chars and can fail a limit by one.
An unknown criterion type silently becomes a FAIL (ok = False) rather than an error, so a typo in a quest file makes every submission fail with no explanation.

check() indexes quest["acceptance_criteria"], c["type"] and c["description"] directly: a missing field raises KeyError, and an empty criteria list yields no results, so the CLI's all([]) passes and exits 0 for any submission.
Quest JSON and CLI args are not validated: a missing argument gives IndexError, and a missing 'value' on contains/max_chars/min_chars gives None, which raises TypeError at comparison.

The criterion types (contains, max_chars, min_chars) are hardcoded here and used by the quest files; adding or renaming one must be done on both sides. 'contains' is case-sensitive and counts Python characters, not bytes.

groups.title: Quest definitions: JSON files with a title and acceptance_criteria for checker.py

checks.why: summary.json loaded and checked through check()

risks.text: Each criterion needs type, value and description; the checker only understands contains, max_chars and min_chars. Any other type always fails.
tagline.json has no test: only summary.json is exercised by tests/test_checker.py, so mistakes in it go unnoticed.
Limits are in characters of the raw file text, including any trailing newline (e.g. summary's 280 limit).

groups.title: pytest tests for check() using the real quest files

risks.text: Tests import checker by editing sys.path to the repo root and open quest files with no encoding, so moving checker.py or quests/ breaks them.
Only the summary quest and two cases are covered: no test for min_chars, unknown types, empty criteria, or the CLI/file input path.
README is the only statement of the contract ('every quest has at least one checkable criterion'); the code does not enforce it, so a quest with an empty criteria list passes everything.

rules.rule: Every quest file must have at least one checkable acceptance criterion, using only the types checker.py supports.
rules.why: An empty list makes the CLI pass every submission, and an unsupported type makes every submission fail.

rules.rule: The CLI exits 0 only if all criteria passed, otherwise 1, and prints PASS/FAIL per criterion description.
rules.why: Callers and scripts rely on the exit status to accept or reject a submission.
